2001 Studio Album 14 Songs

Midnight Drivers

The 2001 Nocturnal Highway Album

The lost 1987 sophomore concept album. Rejected by Apex Records for its moody, atmospheric Darkwave tone, the master tapes sat in the vault for over a decade. Resurrected and released independently by Engine Room Records in 2001, this album finally bridges the gap between the vibrant city lights of Side A and the isolating sanctuary of Side B.

2003 Studio Album 10 Songs

Mile Marker 98

The 2003 "Twin Moons" Project (Moon 2)

The second half of the 2003 'Twin Moons' project. Acting as the 'Engine', this album features exclusively male vocals from Ryan O'Connell. Stripping away the celestial calm, it unleashes blistering, distorted electric guitars and aggressive rock energy. Released simultaneously with its twin, it explores the destructive side of gravity and serves as a heavy, visceral confrontation with the Crash of '90.

2003 Studio Album 10 Songs

Sanctuary (Zero-G)

The 2003 "Twin Moons" Project (Moon 1)

The first half of the 2003 'Twin Moons' project. Acting as the 'Anchor', this album features exclusively female vocals from Cassidy O'Connell. It is the ultimate showcase of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™—a mathematically precise, zero-gravity atmospheric masterpiece recorded while the band constructed their permanent Blacksburg studio. It represents finding a peaceful, silent sanctuary in the endless black.

2004 Studio Album 11 Songs

Progress Street

The 2004 Blacksburg Homecoming Album (Final Release Before the Burnout Hiatus)

A heartfelt, 1980s-inspired AOR and stadium synth-rock album from The Stardust Engine, recorded in 2004 at their home on Progress Street NE in Blacksburg, Virginia. Making the full-blooded 1980s melodic rock record that Apex Records never let them make in 1987, Progress Street celebrates collegiate roots, upright pianos, second-hand 1984 synthesizers, and unbreakable family unity—immortalized on the cover alongside the band's brand-new custom 2004 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 low-floor shuttle coach before exhaustion forced them into their Burnout Hiatus.

2011 Studio Album 14 Songs

Starfield Calibration

Celebrating 25 Years Since Ignition (The Forger's Call) Shook The Crucible (Oct 18, 1986 – Oct 18, 2011)

Released on Tuesday, October 18, 2011—at the midpoint of the band's Burnout Hiatus and on the exact 25th Anniversary of 'Ignition (The Forger's Call)' making its thunderous Saturday night debut inside The Crucible on October 18, 1986—Starfield Calibration reimagines fourteen foundational Stardust Engine classics (1987–2001) entirely within 'The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™' (a proprietary trademark of Michael P. Ragsdale / RaggieSoft Media / Engine Room Records™; '80s Cosmic Pop' is the open generic genre name free for everyone to use). Featuring driving 4/4 gated percussion, shimmering analog synthesizers, Evan Wright's melodic fretless basslines, and lush zero-gravity spatial reverb, this silver-anniversary hiatus release reminded Forger Nation that the family was still in orbit.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)
